title_en: Notice of the General Office of the Supreme People's Court on Matters Concerning Fees for Service of Civil and Commercial Documents Abroad
full_text_en:
Notice of the General Office of the Supreme People's Court

on Matters Concerning Fees for Service of Civil and Commercial Documents Abroad

Fa Ban [2003] No. 242

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government:

Effective June 1, 2003, the United States has authorized a private service company, PROCESS FORWARDING INTERNATIONAL (PFI), to perform part of the functions of the Central Authority of the United States under the Hague Service Convention for a period of five years, and to charge execution fees for each service request directed to its nationals. Since China and Singapore have been handling judicial assistance matters through the channels provided for in the bilateral Treaty on Judicial Assistance between China and Singapore, the Singaporean side has, in accordance with the provisions of Article 10 of the Sino-Singapore Treaty, required payment of execution fees after service has been effected in respect of China's requests for service on its nationals. Canada, in accordance with the provisions of the Hague Service Convention, has declared that it will charge fees to countries requesting judicial assistance. In practice, it has also actually charged fees for China's requests for service on its nationals. The specific requirements for payment of service fees for the above three countries are hereby notified as follows:

I. Specific Requirements for Payment of Service Execution Fees to the United States:

Time of Payment: Prepayment

Method of Payment: Bank draft

Amount of Payment: USD 89 (2003), USD 91 (2004), USD 93 (2005), USD 95 (2007)

Payee of the draft: "PROCESS FORWARDING INTERNATIONAL" (USA)

II. Specific Requirements for Payment of Service Execution Fees to Singapore:

Time of Payment: Payment after execution

Method of Payment: Bank draft

Amount of Payment: The amount charged varies according to the service situation (ranging from SGD 20 to SGD 130 or higher)

Payee of the draft: "The Registrar, Supreme Court, Singapore"

III. Specific Requirements for Payment of Service Fees to Canada:

Time of Payment: Prepayment

Method of Payment: Bank draft

Amount of Payment: CAD 50

Payee of the draft: Fill in the different names according to the different provinces as follows:

Alberta: Provincial Treasurer of Alberta
British Columbia: Minister of Finance of British Columbia
Prince Edward Island: Provincial Treasurer of Prince Edward Island
Manitoba: Minister of Finance of Manitoba
New Brunswick: Minister of Finance of New Brunswick
Nova Scotia: Minister of Finance of Nova Scotia
Ontario: Treasurer of Ontario
Quebec: Ministre des Finances du Quebec
Saskatchewan: Department of Justice of Saskatchewan - Sheriff Services
Newfoundland: Newfoundland Exchequer Account
Yukon Territory: Treasurer of the Government of Yukon
Northwest Territories: Government of the Northwest Territories
Nunavut: Government of Nunavut

Please have the relevant departments of each Higher People's Court handle this accordingly. For service on the United States and Canada, send the bank draft together with the documents for service to the Foreign Affairs Bureau of the Supreme People's Court for forwarding. For service on Singapore, after the documents have been served, pay the service fee as determined by the Singaporean side; the bank draft shall be forwarded through the Foreign Affairs Bureau of the Supreme People's Court.

The party requesting service may, in accordance with the notice issued by our court forwarding the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (Fa [2003] No. 73), apply to the local foreign exchange administration department to purchase the required foreign exchange and arrange for the relevant bank draft.

July 29, 2003
